notes:
# A recording that would not start {camcorder}
Pressing record on a meeting you were already in could end with no
recording at all. The app sends a Return to get past Zoom's join preview,
and it was sending it into the live meeting instead -- four times, one
every six seconds, and then giving up without recording a thing. Whether
it happened came down to which window had focus at that second, which is
why it looked intermittent rather than broken. The key is only sent now
when there is a join preview in front of it.

# A share that recorded black, and nothing knew {film}
A shared screen could still come back black, with the audio running the
whole way through. Everything the run could see said it was fine: the
meeting window stayed in the on-screen list at full size, and that Mac's
share furniture was not recognised, so both of the checks that were meant
to catch this were blind. The capture now watches its own frame count --
one frame a second where fifteen were asked for is a recording of nothing,
whatever Zoom says about its windows -- and follows the screen instead.

# Silencing the meeting actually silences it now {speaker}
The last release announced this and it did not work: the switch went on,
the log said the meeting was muted, and the meeting played on. One flag was
set the wrong way round, and its name reads backwards -- what it did was
mute every app on the Mac EXCEPT Zoom, which is invisible unless something
else happens to be playing. It is measured now rather than assumed: the
room goes from -29 dB to -50 dB the moment the switch goes on, the
recording keeps every word at full level, and the sound is back within a
second of switching it off.

---

Everything else in this release:

- The silencer follows Zoom when Zoom starts another audio process
  part-way through a call -- a screen share brings one up -- instead of
  holding a grip on whatever was making the sound when you flipped the
  switch.
- It can also tell "muted a meeting nobody is talking in" from "muted the
  wrong thing", by measuring what it hears rather than asking macOS
  whether Zoom is playing: that question answers yes through a silent
  meeting, and it is what made a working mute look broken.
- The permission macOS asks for to take Zoom's sound off the speakers is
  now asked for with a reason on it, instead of a bare prompt.
